summary: Field concordance and immutable SIEM snapshot request for tenant export (custodian proof)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MedicaOne Health, enterprise) requests a one-off SIEM snapshot export for a tenant as part of a pending regulatory review. They require:
- A field-concordance matrix that maps Redwood audit fields to their Splunk/QRadar field names.
- An immutable snapshot (tarball) containing daily audit slices for tenant 'medicaone-prod-42' for the period 2024-12-01..2025-01-31. The snapshot must include a manifest with cryptographic checksums and a per-file HMAC tied to the tenant GUID.
- Evidence of delivery and a simple custodian-proof (who retrieved the archive, timestamp, and MD5/SHA256 checksums).
Impact:
The customer is in active regulatory discovery with a compliance deadline next week and needs the package to satisfy auditors. No production traffic impact reported, but the request has high urgency for legal/compliance.
Environment:
Production (eu-west), tenant: medicaone-prod-42, audit export pipeline via s3-archive connector, SIEM target: Splunk HEC behind customer's firewall (pull stage).
Desired deliverables:
1) Field concordance CSV with example mapping and sample event row.
2) Signed snapshot tarball (sha256) plus HMAC manifest per file.
3) Delivery receipts (S3 presigned URL logs and transfer confirmation) and a short checklist explaining how to verify checksums locally.
4) Short note on redaction: what fields were redacted/omitted (if any) and why.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Confirm tenant id and retention window with customer (done in initial call).
2) Trigger on-demand audit dump job for tenant medicaone-prod-42 with window 2024-12-01 to 2025-01-31.
3) Package output into tar.gz, compute checksums (sha256 for files, hmac-sha256 tied to tenant key), and write manifest.json alongside.
4) Stage to secure s3 bucket restricted to support and customer.
5) Share presigned URL and receipt, and capture who downloaded the object and when.
logs:

No 5xx or permission errors observed in pipeline traces.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Avery Chen: Opened request after compliance team call. Customer shared desired field list and a signed letter from their legal counsel requesting custody proof.
2025-02-14 - Riley Patel: Assigned. Confirming we can generate per-file HMACs tied to tenant KEK; will coordinate with security to sign manifest.

2025-02-15 - Samira Ortiz (Security): We can compute HMAC-SHA256 using tenant-specific wrap key; need KMS access log export for the day of signing for attestation. Requesting KMS audit window from Eng infra.
2025-02-15 - Customer (MedicaOne): Provided Splunk field mapping spreadsheet and requested that source IPs be preserved in exported events. Asking whether token hashes are reversible in export.

2025-02-16 - Riley Patel: Confirmed token hashes are one-way; we will include original token fingerprint field (non-reversible) and note that PII fields were redacted per policy. Provided draft field concordance and sample event CSV for review.
2025-02-18 - Customer: Acknowledged receipt of sample and requested the final tarball and manifest by EOD 2025-02-18.
investigation_notes:
2025-02-15: Verified export job completed successfully for the requested date range. Export size ~12.4GB compressed.
Trace: export-job-318207 -> archive-creation succeeded.
Hypothesis: No data loss in pipeline; any missing fields are due to redaction policy or event truncation during collection.
2025-02-16: Security validated HMAC construction. Approach: compute sha256(file) and compute HMAC-SHA256 over sha256(file) using tenant KEK with KMS envelope; store both checksum and hmac in manifest. Colleague Samira requested KMS access logs for the envelope key for 2025-02-16..2025-02-18 for attestation.
2025-02-17: Field concordance draft produced. Two fields required manual harmonization: 'request.user.email' -> redwood.user_email_pseudonym and customer wants original email presence. We propose adding 'user_email_fingerprint' (non-reversible) and documenting that original emails are not present in exports by design.
2025-02-18: Per-customer request, added a custodian-proof text file that records the support agent, timestamp (UTC), and S3 presigned URL issuance with expiry. Also collected the S3 access log entry for the presigned URL fetch (customer downloaded on 2025-02-18T16:04:22Z).
resolution:
Workaround/final delivery: Generated tarball medicaone-audit-20241201-20250131.tar.gz, computed sha256 checksums and HMAC-SHA256 using tenant KEK. Manifest file manifest-medicaone-20250131.json included per-file sha256 and hmac entries and a human-readable README with verification steps.
Delivery: Staged to s3://support-exports/medicaone-prod-42/ with presigned URL sent to customer and S3 access log evidence attached.
Follow-ups: 1) Security to provide KMS access log export for the HMAC signing operations (ticket INT-220 created). 2) Product to consider adding an optional 'raw_emails' toggle for privileged export (requires legal review). 3) Create a short KB article for on-demand immutable tenant snapshots with verification steps.
Status: Delivered to customer on 2025-02-18; customer acknowledged. Pending INT-220 for KMS log export and a follow-up item for the product team.
